leads.work: Real Time desk deal disputes: rebuilding what happened on undocumented deals (zeroed-out or altered EOL trades, Inc-sheet-only deals), confusion over time zones, requesting tapes, and settling disputes with counterparties
leads.why: Kate Symes reports about 30 counterparty disputes from the first two days after EOL launched, with almost no deal documentation, and asks traders to write notes by hand. Bill makes traders state the time zone on every call because otherwise 'disputes will be numerous'. A trader sent dispute emails straight to El Paso, and a tape review was requested.

leads.work: Preschedule and cash desks emailing the Real Time shift by hand about daily long and short positions from parking and lending deals (deal numbers, hours, delivery points), and Bill sending Kate his own daily short/long notes
leads.why: These emails come almost every day. They often contain errors (wrong deal number or delivery point), which annoyed PGE and led to a long clarification email from Kate. The positions are already in Enpower, so they could be pulled from the system instead of retyped.

leads.work: Month-end prior month adjustments (PMA) review and El Paso annuity true-ups to reconcile checkout differences with Enpower
leads.why: Every month Risk sends a preliminary PMA spreadsheet, Kate checks each charge by hand, and Bill asks about unexplained charges. Several rounds of annuities were entered for 2000 months. Kate's vacation was pushed back so October could be settled.

leads.work: Reconciling CAISO congestion revenue: wheels awarded but missing from the Inc sheet, ISO prices that do not match bids, and back-and-forth with the CAISO
leads.why: This happens repeatedly. Bill emails Darren and Jim Reyes about missing hours and revenue to book, notes the ISO 'is again having difficulties reading our bids', and keeps chasing CAISO contacts. Volume Management has to enter bid prices by hand.

leads.work: Real Time position and report reconciliation (CAPS and Enpower position managers) and testing of the new path confirmation system
leads.why: Bill says a consolidated position manager 'has the potential to improve our reports and reduce our time spent running them', but it was delayed behind FSP. Cara's new path confirmation system needs Real Time testing. Deals are built in CAPS and then in Enpower separately.

leads.work: Forwarding misaddressed email between Bill Williams III (Real Time) and Bill Williams (Technical Assets / Longview project)
leads.why: Bill III keeps receiving Longview project email and has to forward it and ask senders to fix their distribution lists. This happens many times over the period.

leads.work: Manager broadcasting operating notices to the Real Time shift list: counterparty credit status (Sempra in a box, WWP okay, LADWP/Coral), BPA transmission prices, SCID changes, shared logins, system downtime, deal-entry rules, and new counterparty procedures
leads.why: Bill sends frequent manual broadcasts to a 15-person list, and the same SCID notice was re-sent weeks later. A shared reference page or counterparty status feed could replace them.

leads.work: Unify Path Manager: processing steps that are inefficient or not needed (path ID reuse lookup, unused scheduling position window, and so on), plus assigning testers from each desk
leads.why: IT says it is identifying processes that 'could possibly benefit from being rewritten or not even performed'. Schedulers confirm the extra steps slow things down and that old zero paths get reused by mistake. A business lead would need 15–75% of their time.

leads.work: Collecting desk information for the Gas Logistics PowerPoint, with repeated reminders to managers
leads.why: Elizabeth Webb sent the request, then reminders, then chased Daren on his own for the Texas slide.

leads.work: Cleaning up legacy HPL/AEP-related transactions: invoices with no deal, meters and contracts that need re-creating for past months, recreating killed deals, imbalance paybacks, missing meters in production statements, and State/County meter checks
leads.why: Settlement and accounting staff keep asking Daren and Mike Olsen to research old months (March 2000, May 2001, and others), set up missing deals or paths, or decide who is responsible for an invoice. This is manual research across Unify and POPS.

leads.work: Texas GLO deal settlement: origination fee deductions, cost of supply, and which cost centers roll up where
leads.why: Several people go back and forth over GL entries, a possible PMA, and whether the costs are entered by hand in Gas Accounting.

leads.work: Correcting counterparty and entity names on booked deals (IDACORP assignments, TXU Gas Distribution, Enbridge Consumers Gas)
leads.why: Mass emails ask traders to book trades with the right counterparty, and specific Sitara deals have to be changed by hand. This points to weak counterparty validation at booking.

leads.work: Recurring reports compiled by hand: the weekly California Capacity Report, the Texas daily gas flow report and fundamentals web page, and monthly budget-vs-actual reports
leads.why: The California report is built every week from El Paso/TW deliveries, Gas Daily prices, and EOL bases. The Texas daily report and analysis is a new assignment for Troy. Budget-vs-actual reports are sent out monthly.

leads.work: Monthly TW rate matrix posting plus a second rate matrix that may no longer be used
leads.why: Rita keeps up a second matrix and says 'I don't know whether anyone needs/uses it, anymore', so it may be work that can be dropped.

leads.work: FERC requirement to file the actual negotiated rate within one day each time an indexed rate changes
leads.why: Mary Kay Miller calls it an 'administrative nightmare' with daily filings for the TW-USGT and NNG-Reliant deals, and suggests posting the rate on the website instead.

leads.work: Collecting OneOk underpaid invoices (force majeure dispute)
leads.why: The receivable has been outstanding since July after unanswered calls, and AR keeps following up.

leads.work: Customer and contact tracking in spreadsheets in place of a CRM, and choosing between Siebel CRM and ACT
leads.why: The origination team spent weeks rebuilding customer contact history and is tracking business in several spreadsheets. Six other groups have asked about the CRM.

leads.work: Handling EES transactions and data: tiered fee calculations, the daily EES data spreadsheet mail-out, and fee negotiations
leads.why: Kysa sends a daily EES spreadsheet by email, and Kate sends EES hourly data separately. The fee tiers are complex and have exceptions announced case by case by email.

leads.work: Hiring and recruiting administration: job postings, internal transfers, resume routing, interview feedback, campus visits, and the new hiring approval sign-off policy
leads.why: Many emails about each candidate. The new policy requires written justification, several sign-offs, and a face-to-face meeting for every replacement hire.

leads.work: Training enrollment and scheduling (Energy Math, Derivatives II, Options, Lexis-Nexis)
leads.why: Managers pick attendees by hand and send email signups, there are waitlist changes, and no-shows are charged.

leads.work: Surveys of schedulers by spreadsheet and BCP seat testing (contingency planning)
leads.why: Each scheduler fills in a spreadsheet that Richard Pinion merges by hand into a master sheet. BCP seats have to be tested weekly.

leads.work: Meeting rescheduling chains run by assistants
leads.why: One strategy meeting was moved four times by email.

leads.work: Customer requests for market data, quotes, and hedge pricing (historical Henry Hub/Ventura prices, swap quotes, prepay pricing)
leads.why: GRE asks for help 'periodically' with gas market data. Hedge quotes and contact reports are prepared and passed between people by hand.

leads.work: System access and IT setup requests (EOL, FSP, Enpower install, profile rebuilds, turret IDs)
leads.why: Bill sends these one at a time, and new hires had trouble getting FSP access.

leads.work: Announcements of IT changes and outages (email address standardization, weekend system availability, office move)
leads.why: Recurring company-wide notices. The email address migration means every employee has to update business cards and notify external contacts.

leads.work: Prioritizing pipeline critical notices for the Fundamentals page
leads.why: Managers mark up a spreadsheet of pipeline notice websites by hand, which suggests notices are being monitored manually.

leads.work: Covering the Alberta desk and following the EPE dispatch rules
leads.why: A memo was needed for weekend coverage. EPE complains about inefficient dispatch, which costs them money (about $1,000 lost per sale).

leads.work: Submitting data to the Powerdex hourly index
leads.why: A proposed daily filing of trade data would be new recurring work for the desk.

leads.work: Revising the mainline expansion cost study
leads.why: Engineering re-ran the scenarios on request to split out interest, overheads, and AFUDC.

leads.work: Month-end close schedule coordination
leads.why: The revised schedule was sent with a request to forward it to anyone left off the list.
